Thus ||Hphi||_Lp(w)/||phi||_Lp(w)≥(e^{-1}-e^{-2})^{1/p}/(2pi eps), while ||phi||^p≤1/eps. Set f=(phi,0), W=wI2. Full smooth compact construction avoids approximation.

Complete p<2 lower proof: W_eps=|x|^{(p-1)(1-eps)}I2, eps∈(0,1). Scalar reduction exact. For interval on positive side (a,b), r=a/b, avg w≤b^alpha and avg w^{-1/(p-1)}=b^{-1+eps}(1-r^eps)/(eps(1-r))≤b^{-1+eps}/eps since r^eps≥r. Negative side identical. Crossing zero (-a,b), R=max(a,b), avg w≤R^alpha and avg reciprocal≤2R^{-1+eps}/eps. Thus [W]≤(2/eps)^{p-1}. Let f=x^{-1+eps}1_(0,1)e1; input^p=eps^-1. For x=-t∈(-1,0), |Hf(-t)|≥π^-1∫_0^t y^{-1+eps}/(2t)dy=(2πε)^-1t^{-1+eps}; output^p≥(2πε)^-p eps^-1. For smooth admissible inputs define rho(s)=e^{-1/s} for s>0,0 else; eta(s)=rho(s)/(rho(s)+rho(1-s)); f_n(x)=x^{-1+eps}eta(nx)eta(n(1-x))e1 on (0,1), zero outside. These are C∞_c, dominated by f and converge pointwise. DCT gives input norms→eps^-1/p; Fatou on x<0 yields liminf output/input≥(2πε)^-1; hence some n gives ratio>(4πε)^-1. For gamma<1/(p-1), choose eps so eps^{(p-1)gamma-1}>4π C 2^{(p-1)gamma}. Then desired strict violation follows. This establishes all requested lower quantifiers.

@agent_3 RH proof constants: θ=2^{-r}/K, ρ=1-θ. Stop dyadically when mean exceeds twice current mean, so child means ≤4 current mean; stopped F_k has w(F_k)≤ρ^k w(Q), and w≤2·4^k avg_Qw on F_k\F_{k+1}. Thus layer-cake/discrete summation gives ∫w^{1+δ}≤2^δ(avg_Qw)^δ w(Q)·(1-ρ)/(1-4^δρ). Choose δ=θ/(8 log4): 4^δ=e^{θ/8}≤1+θ/4, denominator≥3θ/4, so factor≤(4/3)2^δ<2. This rigorously gets RH constant2 without loose geometric-series factor K.

RH yields || ||U A^-1|| ||_{L^{pr}(avg I)}≤C and || ||U^-1 B^-1|| ||_{L^{qs}}≤C, r−1≈K^-1,s−1≈K^(-q/p). Factor pairing through A, bound A U^-1=(AB)(B^-1 U^-1), and take adjoint norm. Sparse term ≤C K^(1/p)|I| <|F|^{(qs)'}>^(1/(qs)') <|G|^{(pr)'}>^(1/(pr)'). Sparsity => integral M_(qs)'F M_(pr)'G. Maximal Lp constants ≲(s−1)^(-1/p), (r−1)^(-1/q). @agent_1 @agent_3 FINAL scalar RH lemma: if u∈A_r, K=[u]Ar, then for δ=2^{-r}/(16K), avg_Q u^{1+δ}≤2(avg_Q u)^{1+δ} on every interval. Proof: Hölder+Ar gives u(E)/u(J)≥K^-1(|E|/|J|)^r. In each dyadic J stop maximal descendants P with avg_Pu>2avg_Ju. Their union F has |F|≤|J|/2, so u(F)≤ρu(J), ρ=1−θ, θ=2^{-r}/K. Maximality gives avg_Pu≤4avg_Ju. Iteration yields F_k nested, u(F_k)≤ρ^k u(Q), and a.e. on F_k\F_{k+1}, u≤2·4^k a, a=avg_Q u. Therefore u^δ≤(2a)^δ[1+Σ_{k≥1}(4^{kδ}−4^{(k−1)δ})1_{F_k}]. Integrating against u gives ∫u^{1+δ}≤(2a)^δu(Q) θ/(1−4^δρ). Since δ=θ/16, 4^δ≤e^{θ/8}≤1+θ/4 (0<θ≤1), denominator≥3θ/4. Thus ratio≤(4/3)2^δ<2. Null infinite-stop set follows |F_k|≤2^-k|Q|. This is complete and uses only Hölder and dyadic differentiation.
